title: Rutford Ice Stream Flow & Tidal Flexure
headline: InSAR velocity fringes track fast Antarctic ice stream surging at over 400 meters per year.
story: The Rutford Ice Stream drains a massive sector of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet into the Ronne Ice Shelf. Flowing at speeds exceeding 400 meters per year, it is governed by subglacial bed conditions and tidal bending at the grounding zone. NISAR's L-band radar penetrates deep into dry polar snow and firn, preserving radar coherence over weeks to measure ice stream velocities and grounding line migration.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Antarctica experiences months of uninterrupted polar night and relentless blizzards. Radar produces daylight-quality imagery and sub-millimeter motion measurements year-round.

story_steps.description: Circular flexure fringes capture oceanic ocean tides lifting and bending the floating Ronne Ice Shelf.

story_steps.title: Ice Stream Mass Loss Telemetry
story_steps.description: Precise velocities enable glaciologists to calculate annual ice discharge into the Southern Ocean.
